reverse_dcf.label: Revenue growth the price implies (reverse DCF)
reverse_dcf.formula: PV(g) = enterprise value $5.48T, solved for g between −50% and +100%

inputs.label: Enterprise value (the target)
inputs.source: computed: market value + debt − cash and securities

inputs.label: Revenue (Revenues, derived)

assumptions: Operating margin 65.2%, every year: the trailing operating margin, $197.58B ÷ $302.97B.
Tax on operating profit 21% (the US federal rate, a stated default).

Sales-to-capital 1.47: trailing revenue $302.97B ÷ invested capital $205.76B (equity $228.98B + debt $33.37B − cash and securities $56.59B, 2026-07-26); each dollar of new revenue is assumed to need capital at this ratio.
Discount rate 9% a year (a stated default, near a long-run US equity return).
After 10 years, growth of 3% a year forever.
Cash flow = revenue × margin × (1 − tax) − (revenue − last year's revenue) ÷ sales-to-capital; discounted at the end of each year; compared with the enterprise value.
reverse_dcf.reading: At these assumptions the enterprise value of $5.48T needs revenue to grow 13.4% a year for 10 years, from $302.97B to $1.07T. The company's own revenue grew +100.0% a year over its last three fiscal years. The largest revenue any filer reported for 2025 is $716.92B (AMAZON.COM, INC.): the implied year-10 revenue is 1.5 times that. Of 40 ten-year spans of filers that started at its size (revenue of $151.48B to $605.94B; starts 2009 to 2015), 0 grew at least that fast (median 1.3% a year, 90th percentile 8.0%; 4 more could not be followed for ten years). With the operating margin at the industry's median of 4.2% (n = 61, 2025) instead of 65.2%, no growth from −50% to +100% a year reaches the price. With the operating margin at the industry's 90th percentile of 26.6% (n = 61, 2025) instead of 65.2%, the same price needs 28.1% a year. Across the grid (discount rate ±2 points, margin ±5 points) the implied growth runs from 6.5% to 19.7% a year (15 of 15 cells solve).
